name: STS-81 rendezvous with Mir (fly_rndz134.py --mission)
notes: Ti = OMS-7 015:01:13:54.1 (Mission Report); epoch = Ti - 68 min, ten minutes before NH (015:00:16:12 RCS).  Target line: Mir's last element set before capture, SGP4 to the epoch, lvlh attitude, no docking port yet (HANDOFF-MIR-STS81.md step 4: the port axis is -Z in portview's Mir frame, vehdyn's is +X).  TGT sets stay STS-134's: STS-81's MC-1/2/3 at Ti+22/52/62 min fit them (T1 20, 49.9 with EL 29.07, +17), not otherwise checked. approach rbar: the Docking Module's axis is the nadir (the Shuttle docks from below, tail forward: Flight Plan JSC-48000-81 p. 8-3 'Docking Att, Tail Fwd, +ZLV -XVV', LVLH R180 P180 Y0), so the port's up is Mir -X. epoch moved to 00:21:00 (Ti-52.9 min): the flown burn table's NH (00:16:12) is carried by the physics (make_return_start --burn), not flown by the driver. midcourse 3: STS-81 flew MC-1/2/3 (015/01:36:06, 02:06:16, 02:16:00 = Ti+22.2, +52.4 min and MC2+9.73 min); the TGT sets keep STS-134's offsets and DTs (STS-81's are not in any document here) with the flown times as T1; set 13's T2 is the R-bar point 600 ft below. START: the Orbiter's state at the 00:21:00 epoch is Mir's (TLE) plus the designed relative state (rndz_start.py; the same Ti-point geometry that reproduces the flown Ti of 9.5 ft/s), not the physics carry of the flown OMS-3..NH burns: those are ground-targeted from tracking and the carry (burn_chain.py, documented in HANDOFF-MIR-STS81) misses the phase by ~27 deg although it reproduces the documented apsides after NC5/NC6 to ~3 nmi with OMS-3 x1.22. set 13 (MC-3): T2 = MC-3 + 10 min = Ti+72 min, the Flight Plan's ESTABLISH RBAR (JSC-48000-81 p. 8-3 row 23, MET 1/17:15 = Ti+72 min) at the RBAR ARRIVAL range of 1000 ft (LOW Z from 1000 ft, p. 49). set 13 back to STS-134's offsets (-900 ft, +1800 ft) at MC-3 + 10 min = Ti+72 (the Flight Plan's ESTABLISH RBAR time): a 1000 ft R-bar aim needed 5.5 ft/s where the flight burned 0.2; the manual RBAR leg then flies to the R-bar at 1000 ft.

undock.note: Mission Report: ODS powered 020:01:46:24, undocking complete 020:02:15:24, then a fly-around (not flown here) and the +X separation 3.0 ft/s at 020:04:02:00 (flown here 15 min after the undock instead: no fly-around leaves nothing to hold the Orbiter near Mir for 1h45m). FREE/hook/pulse GMTs follow STS-134's offsets (FREE = hook-40 s; hook = undock complete - 127 s).

return.note: Mission Report: deorbit TIG 022:13:17:33.2 (355.8 ft/s, dual engine), landing KSC 33 022 14:22:44 GMT.  The planner takes the pass nearest that landing and puts EI 4,400 n.mi. from the runway (STS-134's 4,393-4,438); an EI pinned 31.7 min before the landing with the simulated orbit's phase gave REI 7,690 n.mi., an entry that cannot reach the runway.  gamma_ei -1.37 is the value at which the planner's burn is the flown 355.8 ft/s (-0.96, STS-134's design value, gave 270 ft/s and an entry that skipped out at perigee near the 51.6 deg latitude turning point).

tgt_sets_note: EXPERIMENT (rr14): every set aims at T2 = Ti+72.1 = the flown MC3 TIG (Ti+62.13) + STS-134's 10 min DT, which is the Flight Plan's ESTABLISH RBAR at Ti+72 (pp. 47-49): TGT 10 DT 72.1, set 11 DT 49.9 (22.2+49.9), set 12 DT 19.7 (52.4+19.7), set 13 DT 10.  Before: T2 = Ti+76.9 (STS-134's), rr12/13.  rr18: the aim is now ON the R-bar, 1000 ft below (DX 0, DZ +1.0 kft): Flight Plan pp. 3-14 'RBAR ARRIVAL (DAP LOW Z 1000 ft)' at MET 1/17:15 = Ti+72, the tail-forward maneuver at 17:23 (Ti+80), 170 ft stationkeeping at 17:39 (Ti+96), 100 ft at 18:10 (Ti+127), 30 ft at 18:25 (Ti+142), contact 18:44 (Ti+161) (3 px/min on the page).  With that aim the Ti burn is 9.85 ft/s at best (Ti point -84 kft; flown 9.5).
apds_waits_note: STS-81 flew capture 03:54:50 -> docking complete 04:02:43 (7.9 min, Mission Report); the ISS-era cards' crew waits (90, 30, 30 s) gave 10.3 min with the mechanism's own 198 s ring-in and the hooks.  No STS-81 card is available: these shorter waits are a CALIBRATION to the flown duration, not sourced.
ti_point_note: CALIBRATION: with every set aimed at T2 = Ti+72.1 (the Flight Plan's ESTABLISH RBAR at Ti+72) STS-134's Ti point (-48.6 kft, 1.2 kft below) gives a 10.58 ft/s Ti burn in PASS (rndz_start's Lambert: 10.44); the flown OMS-7 was 9.5 ft/s.  -66.04 kft behind gives 9.50 in the Lambert scan (tools/rndz_start.py functions, DT 72.1, aim -0.9,0,1.8 kft).  No source gives STS-81's Ti point.
final_fps_note: PACING: the 30 -> 10 ft closing slowed from 0.07 to 0.04 ft/s so that CAPTURE comes at the flown Ti+160.9 (rr18/dk19: aligned at 30 ft Ti+150.4 = the Flight Plan's NORM Z at ~151, capture Ti+156.7); the plan puts contact at 1/18:44 'SHK AOS +3 min'.
takeover_note: Manual takeover 5 min after MC-3's TIG (Ti+67), when the Orbiter is about 2,800 ft below (JSC-63400 Fig 20.17: 'manual takeover about 2,800 ft below ... braking gates 2,000-1,200 ft'); before, the manual phase began at T2 (Ti+72.2) 878 ft out with 5 ft/s of closing, overshot to 632 ft and took 11 min to settle.
orbiter_kg_note: vehdyn's ORBITER_KG is the Orbiter with FULL OMS and RCS, from which the propellant used is then subtracted (OMS_USED_LB, RCS_USED_LB); it was given 105,600 (the mass at Ti), so the typed STS-134 OMS use (15.7 klb) was subtracted again and the sim's Orbiter weighed 97,284 kg at Ti (the Ti burn lasted 10.0 s against the flown 12.0 s).  Now: A-6's 242,178 lb at insertion = 109,847 kg, less the STS-81 burns' OMS propellant before Ti at 19.32 lb/s per engine (OMS-2, OMS-3, OMS-5, OMS-6 both engines 47.6+51.4+58.5+63.3 = 220.8 s, NC-2 right engine 10.0 s: L 4,266 lb, R 4,459 lb) and the typed RCS use: about 105,380 kg at Ti (the ascent's own 8 klb consumption is already in the 242,178).
